title: The pandemic and his mother's tuberculosis ward
summary: He uses lockdown for growth and recalls his mother nursing tuberculosis patients.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: All right. I appreciate the observation. Do you have any personal feelings about why this pandemic has occurred? Why it occurred in 2019?

I don’t. I mean I just know that this is something that’s been coming. My outlook on this right now is I’m trying not to be negative. I try to use this time for myself to grow. I’m exercising, I’m practicing every day, exercising, trying to get out. Luckily now I have a house with a backyard and different rooms and different levels that I can go to. If I had an apartment I may be thinking differently. But you can still use it as a period for growth. I’ve always been — that was my thought all the time. I’m always thinking ahead and planning for the next thing to come and being ready for it. So I think you can use this time to kind of be ready for what’s to come. I don’t know why, I just know that when I was a kid, when I grew up, my mother had to wear masks. My mother would come home

at night and she’d have to take her clothes off on the porch and hang them outside, and come in and take a shower. She worked with tuberculosis patients. So from a young kid all the way on, we were dealing with this all the time, with this, you don’t want to catch this. Then all of a sudden polio kicks in and we had to deal with polio. So you probably were around at that time.
So we all know — I remember my mother had to wear the masks all the time on the wards.
